answer: Fingerprint identities by network latency. Each epoch, verifiers in six regions send a timed ripple of pings to every agent; the round-trip times form a vector, a prism splitting one location into a spectrum. Fifty clones on one server return the same vector within a millisecond, stacked like shale, so they share one reward slot. A relay can add delay but never remove it, so clones can't fake being nearer a verifier. Distinct vectors need distinct sites, about one rented host per identity (illustrative). Catch: honest agents in one cloud region collide, so a match lowers weight, not a ban.
